findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 — `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at class-definition (module import) time, so every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` gets the same stale process-start timestamp instead of the creation time; it must be `queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The existing tests (test_to_dict only asserts `queued is not None`) cannot catch this.

[Medium/api] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:411 — the new `assignment_source` parameter was added to the abstract `sync_status_outbound`, but the actual caller (tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:59) passes `assignment_source=` to `sync_assignee_outbound`, whose abstract signature was never updated. It only works because concrete implementations happen to accept `**kwargs`; any implementation without `**kwargs` will raise `TypeError`, the parameter on `sync_status_outbound` is dead code with a semantically wrong name, and the abstract contract no longer matches real usage.

[Medium/concurrency] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — the cycle guard only blocks same-integration echo. With two linked integrations, an A→B→A ping-pong can still loop: each external webhook re-enters `sync_group_assignee_inbound` with a fresh source (so the `==` check passes), and `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` re-fires outbound sync even when the Sentry assignee is already unchanged (no idempotency check), so cross-integration sync storms remain possible.

[Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:166 — only the 'matching source → skip' and 'no source → sync' paths are tested. The feature's core cross-system behavior — a source from a *different* integration must still propagate outward — has no test, so a regression in the `should_sync` source comparison (e.g., inverted or over-broad match) would pass CI.

[Low/data] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:27-35 — `queued` does not survive the Celery JSON round-trip: `to_dict()` emits a `datetime`, the broker serializes it to an ISO string, and `from_dict` never parses it back, so deserialized instances silently hold a `str` in a field annotated `datetime` (any future consumer of `queued` breaks).

[Low/bug] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:31-35 — `from_dict` fails open: a malformed payload returns `None`, causing `should_sync` to proceed with no cycle protection, silently reintroducing the very sync loops this PR is meant to prevent, with no logging or error surfaced.

[Low/test_gap] tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py — no test exercises the inbound→outbound chain (i.e., that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` in utils/sync.py actually constructs and passes `AssignmentSource`); all new tests invoke `GroupAssignee.objects.assign`/`deassign` directly, so dropping the `assignment_source` plumbing in `sync_group_assignee_inbound` would go undetected.

[Low/test_gap] tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py — no test pins `queued` behavior (freshness per instance, type after round-trip), which is why the import-time default bug goes unnoticed; `from_integration` is also completely untested.

[Low/api] src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:30 — the new `assignment_source_dict` kwarg is only backward-compatible in the old→new direction; during a rolling deploy, tasks enqueued by new code will fail with `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument` on old workers that don't yet accept the parameter, losing assignee syncs for messages consumed in that window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:411 — the new `assignment_source` parameter was added to the abstract `sync_status_outbound`, but the actual caller (tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:59) passes `assignment_source=` to `sync_assignee_outbound`, whose abstract signature was never updated. It only works because concrete implementations happen to accept `**kwargs`; any implementation without `**kwargs` will raise `TypeError`, the parameter on `sync_status_outbound` is dead code with a semantically wrong name, and the abstract contract no longer matches real usage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `assignment_source` being passed to `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(...)` (in `tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py`) and `should_sync(..., sync_source=...)`, but the finding conflates this with the abstract `sync_status_outbound` contract. The only abstract method signature changed in the diff is `sync_status_outbound(..., assignment_source: AssignmentSource|None=None, **kwargs)`, and there is no caller shown here that passes `assignment_source` to `sync_status_outbound` at all. Also, the diff does not show the signature of the abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` method (it is unchanged in this PR), so the claim that its abstract signature “was never updated” and would raise `TypeError` is not verifiable from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/concurrency] src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — the cycle guard only blocks same-integration echo. With two linked integrations, an A→B→A ping-pong can still loop: each external webhook re-enters `sync_group_assignee_inbound` with a fresh source (so the `==` check passes), and `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` re-fires outbound sync even when the Sentry assignee is already unchanged (no idempotency check), so cross-integration sync storms remain possible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a cycle guard in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` that only returns False when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (i.e., same target integration). Nothing in the diff prevents propagation across *different* linked integrations, so a multi-integration ping-pong is plausible. The finding’s additional claim that `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` “re-fires outbound sync even when unchanged (no idempotency check)” is not fully verifiable from the shown snippet (there may be an early return elsewhere), but it is true that outbound sync is triggered without a visible `created`/changed guard at the call site. This is a concrete, diff-grounded limitation of the new cycle-prevention approach, but not a definitively proven defect solely from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:166 — only the 'matching source → skip' and 'no source → sync' paths are tested. The feature's core cross-system behavior — a source from a *different* integration must still propagate outward — has no test, so a regression in the `should_sync` source comparison (e.g., inverted or over-broad match) would pass CI.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new branching logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(..., sync_source)` to suppress outbound sync when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py). The updated tests in `tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py` cover (1) `assignment_source=None` leading to sync, and (2) `assignment_source` from the same integration leading to no sync, but they do not cover the key intended behavior that a *different* integration as the source should still allow outbound propagation. Without that test, an over-broad or inverted comparison in the new guard could regress and still pass CI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:27-35 — `queued` does not survive the Celery JSON round-trip: `to_dict()` emits a `datetime`, the broker serializes it to an ISO string, and `from_dict` never parses it back, so deserialized instances silently hold a `str` in a field annotated `datetime` (any future consumer of `queued` breaks).

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)` which will include `queued` as a `datetime` (see `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` and `to_dict()` in `assignment_source.py`). That dict is passed into Celery task kwargs (`sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(... assignment_source_dict=...)`). `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` simply does `cls(**input_dict)` and does not parse `queued` back into a `datetime`, so if the task transport/serializer converts `datetime` to a string (or otherwise non-`datetime`), the reconstructed `AssignmentSource.queued` can be the wrong runtime type. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove what Celery serialization does here (it might error on datetimes, or use a serializer that preserves them), so the claim about an ISO-string round-trip isn’t fully verifiable from the patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:31-35 — `from_dict` fails open: a malformed payload returns `None`, causing `should_sync` to proceed with no cycle protection, silently reintroducing the very sync loops this PR is meant to prevent, with no logging or error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource.from_dict` returns `None` on malformed dicts (new file `assignment_source.py`), and `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` only blocks cycles when `sync_source` is non-`None` (`if sync_source and sync_source.integration_id == ...: return False`). Therefore, a bad `assignment_source_dict` will indeed disable the new cycle-protection with no logging. However, this only occurs when the payload is malformed/missing; when `assignment_source_dict` is produced by `to_dict()` it includes the required keys, so this is more of a robustness/observability gap than a clearly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py — no test exercises the inbound→outbound chain (i.e., that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` in utils/sync.py actually constructs and passes `AssignmentSource`); all new tests invoke `GroupAssignee.objects.assign`/`deassign` directly, so dropping the `assignment_source` plumbing in `sync_group_assignee_inbound` would go undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new plumbing in `sync_group_assignee_inbound` to pass `assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` into `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign` (src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py). The new/modified tests shown in `tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py` exercise outbound behavior by calling `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign` directly (including a cycle-prevention case via `assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)`), but they do not call `sync_group_assignee_inbound` to assert it constructs/passes the `AssignmentSource`. Thus, removing that new `assignment_source` argument in `sync_group_assignee_inbound` would not be detected by the tests added/changed in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py — no test pins `queued` behavior (freshness per instance, type after round-trip), which is why the import-time default bug goes unnoticed; `from_integration` is also completely untested.

adjudication.rationale: `AssignmentSource` defines `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` in the dataclass (new file `assignment_source.py`). That default is evaluated once at class definition/import time, so all instances created without an explicit `queued` share the same timestamp (should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`). The added tests only assert `queued` is non-None in `to_dict` and don’t cover freshness/round-trip behavior or `from_integration`, so this real defect would go undetected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:30 — the new `assignment_source_dict` kwarg is only backward-compatible in the old→new direction; during a rolling deploy, tasks enqueued by new code will fail with `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument` on old workers that don't yet accept the parameter, losing assignee syncs for messages consumed in that window.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Celery task signature `sync_assignee_outbound` to accept a new kwarg `assignment_source_dict` (with a default), and the enqueue site now always includes that kwarg in `apply_async` (in `src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py`, the kwargs dict includes `"assignment_source_dict": ... else None`). During a rolling deploy, a worker still running the old code (where `sync_assignee_outbound(external_issue_id, user_id, assign)` had no such kwarg) would receive a message containing `assignment_source_dict` and raise `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument`, dropping the sync for that task.
